android.desc:
Drift: Mindful Heart & Stress Monitoring

Understand the language of your heart. Drift is a compassionate companion designed to help you navigate stress, anxiety, and ADHD through the lens of Heart Rate Variability (HRV). In a world that never stops, Drift offers a quiet space to check in with your body. By using professional-grade physiological metrics and a minimalist, low-sensory design, Drift turns your smartphone into a powerful tool for self-regulation and emotional awareness.

Why Drift?

For those living with ADHD or anxiety, traditional health apps can often feel overwhelming or "loud." Drift is built on the philosophy of ilseon; a minimalist aesthetic that focuses on calm, clarity, and compassionate insights. Instead of just giving you numbers, Drift helps you understand what those numbers mean for your day.

Key Features

1. Professional Stress Index Go beyond basic pulse monitoring. Drift calculates your Stress Index using the Kubios-standard (a linearised Baevsky formula) to provide a clear, readable measure of your nervous system's load. • Low Strain / Recovery: Your system is in deep rest—the perfect time for focus. • Active Load: You’re in flow, but don’t forget to breathe. • System Overload: A gentle reminder to scale down and prioritise rest. 2. Precision HRV Monitoring (RMSSD) Measure your Heart Rate Variability (HRV) using the high-precision RMSSD metric. Understand your body’s resilience and its ability to switch between "fight or flight" and "rest and digest." 3. The Energy Orb A central, glowing visual representation of your current state. No complex charts required—simply look at the Orb to see if your energy is in a state of calm, focus, or urgency. 4. Compassionate Insights Drift doesn't just track data; it provides context. If your Stress Index is high, Drift might suggest: "You might just be tired, not stressed." 5. Seamless Sleep Tracking Log your sleep with a single tap. See how your rest directly impacts your morning HRV and stress levels, helping you find the "sweet spot" for your personal recovery. 6. ADHD & Anxiety Friendly • Minimalist UI: Low-sensory design to reduce cognitive load. • Quick-Log Widget: Check in directly from your home screen without opening the app. • Pulse Feedback: Visual pulsing that syncs with your heartb

show_hn.title: Show HN: Drift, an open source HRV reader

quotes.text:
It all started with me wanting to measure my HRV and I tried many different apps but wasn't really impressed, either they came with an expensive subscription or they had a very cluttered interface, and the PPG (photoplethysmography (using the camera)) wasn't that accurate IMHO. A wearable like a smartring or a wristwatch would probably been better but I didn't wanna buy one...

So I started to build my own and it has been an interesting experience, I have been reading a lot about HRV, RR intervals and how to use the baevsky method for figuring out a stress index, fascinating reading.

Drift helps you understand your current capacity by looking at BPM, HRV, SI and amount of sleep per night. Without a wearable one have to manually start tracking sleep but it has a smart feature and will stop tracking after first unlock in the morning (it waits 2 hours for late night scrollers to make sure you're sleeping)

I didn't find any good open source apps for this so hopefully Drift gets some traction for the ones interested.

I'm a strong believer in OSS and I think users will like the openness of being able to see what's going on, and the convenience of getting it at the Play Store for a low price (no subscriptions or hidden fees).

GitHub (MIT open source): https://github.com/cladam/drift
Play Store: https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.ilseon.drift

Thanks for checking it out.
